terms.gloss: draw up (ships on to the shore); draw away, withdraw, take away quietly
evidence: Liv. 45.42: nāvēs rēgiae in campō Mārtiō subductae sunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 2.40: subdūc cibum ūnum diem āthlētae (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: slip or glide away, slip out, escape
evidence: Plaut. Ps. 2.4.57: anguilla est, ēlābitur (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BC 2.11.1: quicquid incidit, fastīgiō mūsculī ēlābitur (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: take an athlete’s food away for a single day

phrases.latin: magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus
phrases.english: a great part of life slips away from those who do badly, the greatest part from those who do nothing, the whole of it from those who do something else
he’s an eel, he slips away

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 381.
